newsitem.title: USA: Texas property tax vote postponed to Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Texas property tax vote postponed to Wednesday.

text.p: Texas House Speaker Pete Laney postponed Tuesday's much-anticipated vote on property tax cuts after some 235 proposed amendments to the legislation were pre-filed by Monday night's deadline, a spokeswoman for his office said.
The vote is now expected on Wednesday.
"By the first deadline at five o'clock (1600 EDT) yesterday there was a line out the door to the chief clerk's office filing those," Janet Warren, press secretary to Laney, a democrat, said.

At the close of Monday's house session, Laney announced that when House Bill Four and House Joint Resolution Four came up for a vote on Tuesday, a motion would be made to postpone the vote until Wednesday, Warren said.

"He just thought in all fairness to the members, for the members benefit, that they (should) be given time to look at those amendments so we can run some fiscal analysis on some of them, etc., etc," the spokeswoman said.
House Bill Four would result in a $1 billion net reduction in property taxes paid by Texans, according to a synopsis of the bill.

The proposal would cut residential rates on average by 50 percent with a cap of 70 cents per $100 for maintenance and operation. It caps business rates at $1.05 per $100. It would also pass property cuts onto renters.
The proposal also calls for the state to pay for 80 percent of public education costs, and would provide state matching funds to help districts retire bond debt and build new facilities.

The plan would pay for the property tax cuts with $1 billion from surplus state funds and by eliminating a variety of exemptions. It would apply franchise tax to partnerships but not sole proprietors. It would eliminate 30 sales tax exemptions, five motor fuels tax exemptions and increase taxes on tobacco products and alcoholic beverages.
HJR Four is a proposed constitutional amendment accompanying House Bill Four that would alter some aspects of the state's constitution to allow for HB Four, Warren said.
